newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises to 8.5 pct on tightness. [corrected 09:45 gmt]
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises to 8.5 pct on tightness. [corrected 09:45 gmt]

text.p: The overnight interbank rate rose to 8.5 percent against 7.5 on Friday on as the market remained tight in afternoon trading, dealers said on Monday.
They said the tightness was caused by Bank Negara's intervention last Thursday and the outgo of overseas funds.
But, some dealers said it was unclear why the interbank rates were rising.
They said there has been some other outflow from the system apart form the intervention to cause such a significant tightening of the market.
Many dealers said the interbank rates would rise further on Tuesday owing to the high overnight rate.
(Corrects to remove reference to Bank Negara issues)
"I am not very clear why the market is tight, but I know the rates will go up further tomorrow," one interbank dealer said.
Earlier, other interbank rates were mostly higher as the market remained tight, dealers said.
One-week money was at 7.10/20 percent against 6.90/7.00, two-week at 7.20 against 7.00/10 and one-month at 7.18/20 against 7.10/15.
Three-month money rose to 7.20/25 against 7.15/20 and six-month to 7.23/26 against 7.20/23.
The forecast in Malaysian Finance Ministry's Economic Report for 1996/97 on Friday that monetary policy would remain tight for the rest of the year had little impact, the dealers said.
